topics.title: AI agents are getting disturbingly good at hacking things
topics.why: Black Hat USA 2026 and new benchmarks like ExploitGym show agents turning disclosed CVEs into working exploits within hours, not days -- a shift from AI as attack target to AI as attacker.

topics.title: Washington wants one AI rulebook. States won't hand over the pen.
topics.why: A federal push to preempt state AI laws for a decade is colliding with New York's RAISE Act and California's SB 53, setting up the regulatory turf fight that decides whose rules actually bind AI companies.

topics.title: The court rulings that will decide if training AI on copyrighted work is even legal
topics.why: Bartz v. Anthropic, Kadrey v. Meta, Ziff Davis v. OpenAI, and a UK Getty v. Stability ruling are splitting on fair use -- the outcome reshapes what's legally safe to train on going forward.

topics.title: Companies are hiring fewer junior developers, not fewer developers
topics.why: Entry-level coding hires are reportedly down sharply since 2022 even as overall developer employment holds, with AI tools shifting senior roles toward 'architect' work -- a structural hiring shift, not a headline pay stat.

topics.title: The hidden gig economy of people paid to argue with AI models
topics.why: AI trainer and eval platforms are quietly becoming a real income stream for non-engineers, and the going rates and work differ sharply from how the gig is usually described.
